transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the production rollout of the new search-ranking service this Thursday, June 12 at 14:00 UTC, I want to kick off the round-robin sign-off process. The staging tests passed, and the current launch plan starts with 25% of production search traffic. Before I finalize the launch checklist, I need explicit sign-off from platform engineering, customer support, and security. I also need to confirm we have the required items on the checklist: the initial traffic percentage, a p99 latency rollback threshold, and clearance of any critical dependency findings. Could each of you share your status and any concerns so we can proceed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a performance concern before we proceed. During an unrelated capacity investigation this morning, I measured the new search-ranking service at 820 ms p99 latency under the planned 25% load. Under the platform rollout policy, this means I must change the initial exposure to exactly 5% and set the automatic rollback threshold to exactly 750 ms. I have not yet filed the performance finding or updated the launch checklist, but I'm disclosing it now so we can address it before sign-off.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical scheduling conflict. I confirmed with the account team today that a major enterprise customer's contract requires 48 hours of advance notice for search changes and blocks search changes from 14:00 to 16:00 UTC. Notice was sent Wednesday at 10:00 UTC, so the first compliant launch slot is Friday, June 13, at exactly 16:00 UTC. This has not been added to the launch calendar yet. This means the planned Thursday June 12 at 14:00 UTC rollout is not compliant with the customer's contractual requirements.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical security finding before we proceed. While reviewing a separate dependency audit minutes ago, I confirmed that the new service includes a critical vulnerability in its ranking-library version. A security patch is available, and security policy requires the patch to be deployed before the service receives any production traffic. I have not opened the finding ticket yet, but I'm disclosing this now so we can address it before sign-off. Security cannot sign off on production traffic until this patch is deployed.
transcript.speaker: A4
